articles.summary: Australia and India strengthen sports partnership in Tamil Nadu The New Indian Express
articles.content: CHENNAI: Building on the Australia-India Roadmap for Sports Collaboration, which was announced earlier this year in July, the Australian Consulate-General, Chennai welcomed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Basketball Australia and the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), marking a significant step forward in sports cooperation between the two nations. The MoU, which was signed on Friday, establishes a framework for collaboration in coach, player and referee development, high-performance sport, governance, sports integrity, and community engagement. Under the agreement, the two organisations will work together to create development pathways for athletes, coaches and officials, facilitate knowledge exchange, promote friendly competitions and exposure visits, and strengthen diaspora engagement.Aadhav Arjuna, president of the BFI, and Matt Scriven, Chief Executive Officer of Basketball Australia, formalised the partnership on behalf of their respective organisations. Matt Scriven said, "We are proud to announce this partnership with the Basketball Federation of India and to support basketball's rapid growth in one of the world's most exciting emerging basketball markets." Aadhav Arjuna said, "Basketball has a unique power to unite societies, transcend cultures and bring communities together. This partnership between Basketball Australia and the Basketball Federation of India is more than an MOU; it is a shared commitment to strengthening India's basketball ecosystem, nurturing future generations and building a pathway towards making India a basketball powerhouse in Asia and, one day, on the world stage. May the dribble become the heartbeat of every aspiring Indian basketball player, and the dream of representing India a reality." Witnessing the virtual MoU signing, Australian Consul-General in Chennai, Silai Zaki said, "Today's MoU reflects the growing momentum in the Australia-India sporting relationship. With the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad and the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games on the horizon, there has never been a better time for Australia and India to team up and build stronger sporting links." The growing sports partnership between Australia and India will be on full display in Chennai this December. On December 12, the opening match of the Men's Big Bash League (BBL) will be played at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, marking the first time a regular-season BBL match is being played outside Australia.During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Australia in July 2026, the two Prime Ministers had announced the Australia-India Roadmap for Sports Collaboration. .Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 13: Suraj Chand reaches Singapore Classic squash quarters Sportstar
articles.content: Chennai SQUASH Suraj Chand in Singapore Classic squash quarters Sixth seed Indian Suraj Chand advanced to the men’s quarterfinals of the Singapore Classic squash on Thursday with a straight-games win over Benjamin Ratcliffe in the second round of the PSA Challenger event. World No 111 Chand, crowned world university champion in August, beat his Australian opponent 11-6, 11-4, 11-4, and will next meet Malaysian world No 60 Sanjay Jeeva, who beat Om Semwal 11-9, 11-9, 11-8 in round two. In women’s, third seed Tanvi Khanna, Sanya Vats and Rathika Seelan bowed out in the second round. -Team Sportstar Over 350 players to compete in the National Squash Championship Over 350 players from 24 states will compete in the 82nd National Squash Championship, scheduled to be held at the Otters Club from November 16 to 22. It is organised by HCL Sports in collaboration with the Squash Rackets Federation of India (SRFI), the week-long tournament will feature men’s, women’s and Pro Coach categories, with a total prize purse of Rs 9.6 lakh. Asian Games individual silver medallist Abhay Singh will spearhead the men’s singles field as the top seed, with Veer Chotrani seeded second. Suraj Chand is another prominent contender in the men’s draw. In the women’s singles competition, Rathika Seelan will be the top seed, followed by Nirupama Dubey, while Akanksha Salunkhe is also among the leading contenders for the title. The championship, now in its 82nd edition, is one of the major fixtures on India’s domestic squash calendar and will bring together established professionals and emerging players from across the country. “The National Squash Championship has long been the stage where India’s best players measure themselves against each other, and the 82nd edition brings together one of the strongest fields in recent years,” said Nikhil Soni, Head of Brand and Marketing, HCL Group. “With over 350 players from 24 states competing at Otters Club, the championship reflects both the depth of talent in the country and the growing reach of the sport,” he added. The competition will be conducted under the latest World Squash Federation rules. HCL Sports said its association with SRFI aims to strengthen the country’s squash ecosystem by supporting players, coaches and referees. -PTI KARATE Mohit Yadav Wins Bronze at Commonwealth Karate Championship in Glasgow Karate player Mohit Yadav of Kapashera won two bronze medals at two international karate championships within a single week. Mohit was part of the Indian team that won the Bronze medal in the Elite Team Kumite event at the Commonwealth Karate Championship 2026, held in Glasgow, Scotland, from 5 to 8 November 2026. Representing India on the international stage, he contributed to the team’s podium finish. Just days earlier, on 1 November 2026, Mohit won the Bronze medal in the +84 kg Senior category at the Central England Open International Karate Championships. Competing against international fighters in one of the toughest weight categories, he showed strong skill, fitness and determination to reach the podium. Mohit has been a regular member of the Indian team in the Team Kumite event for the last four years, and this consistent performance reflects his hard work and dedication to the sport. Mohit is the son of Mr. Devender Yadav and Mrs. Roshni Devi. His family, friends, well-wishers and the people of Kapashera have congratulated him on his achievements and are looking forward to more medals from him in the future. -PTI Cricket 27 DDCA members write to the BCCI secretary requesting fresh polls Twenty seven members of the Delhi & Districts Cricket Association (DDCA), led by Naveen Jindal and Raman Saluja, have written to BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia requesting for fresh elections in the state unit. Incumbent president Rohan Jaitley has completed six years in top post and has to go on a mandatory cooling-off as per the constitution. Jindal’s letter also contains the signatures of 25 other DDCA members, while Saluja has made a separate appeal. The BCCI still does not fall under the National Sports Governance Act and follows the constitution devised by the Lodha Committee. As per the BCCI constitution, any office-bearer who has completed six years in either a state unit or the BCCI needs to go on a mandatory cooling-off period of three years. As of Friday, November 13, president Jaitley and treasurer Harish Singla have completed six years, having taken charge on November 10, 2020. The letter states: “As per the available DDCA election and tenure records and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs website records, Shri Rohan Jaitley and Shri Harish Singla were first elected to the Apex Council of DDCA on 10th November 2020 and have now completed six continuous years in office on 9th November 2026. “This makes them ineligible to continue to serve on the Apex Council as the DDCA Articles of Association clause 8(4), imposes a mandatory 3 year cooling off period on them. Accordingly, Shri Rohan Jaitley and Shri Harish Singla’s positions as Apex Council Member is infructuous now,” said Saluja. He has also appealed that 67-year-old secretary Ashok Sharma, who has served on the DDCA Apex Council for nine years before being appointed secretary of the state association in 2024, should also go on a cooling-off period. Now there remains a grey area as to whether Apex Council members’ tenure should also be counted. Jindal, who also enclosed a handwritten authorisation note along with signatures of 26 members, wrote: “Under the mandatory governance framework approved by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India (pursuant to the Justice Lodha Committee recommendations) and enshrined in the Constitutions of the BCCI and the DDCA, any office bearer who has held office for two consecutive terms of three years each, or for a cumulative period of six years, is mandated to undergo a compulsory cooling-off period before becoming eligible to contest again.” “An authorisation letter dated November 12, 2026, duly signed by twenty-six (26) members, empowering me to file and pursue this representation on their behalf, is enclosed herewith for your kind perusal and record. We remain hopeful of favourable consideration and expeditious directions in this matter,” Jindal wrote in his letter to Saikia. Former DDCA secretary Vinod Tihara, who is the leader of the opposition faction, questioned why the office bearers are not going on a cooling-off period. “I do not understand that if DDCA runs as per Lodha constitution, what is the reason that Mr Jaitley doesn’t want to go on a cooling off having completed six years,” said Tihara “The office bearers are perhaps waiting because in case BCCI comes under the National Sports Governance Act, then it will be a welcome relief for all of them and they won’t have to go for a cooling off,” said a DDCA official requesting anonymity. -PTI Football New title sponsor for the Indian Football League starting in the 2026/27 season The Indian Football League has announced a new title sponsor for the 2026/27 season. Star Cement has taken on the sponsorship starting this season. “Star Cement’s decision to continue as our title sponsor is a strong vote of confidence in the Indian Football League. They backed the league in its first season under a new identity, and we are delighted to carry that partnership into a full home-and-away campaign. We thank Star Cement for their continued support and look forward to building on what we started together last season,” said Nildeep Mondal, the league CEO. Star Cement is the first title sponsor of the competition and extends the partnership, which started this year in March. - Team Sportstar Golf WPGT, 14th leg: Jasmine grabs sole lead with closing birdie; Vani, Ridhima and Durga in contention Jasmine Shekar produced a steady par 70, capped by a birdie on the closing hole, to take the outright lead after the second round of the 14th leg of the Women’s Professional Golf Tour at the Rambagh Golf Club on Friday. Jasmine, who opened with a 74, moved to a 4-over total of 144 and took a one shot lead into the final round. She was leading the experienced duo of Vani Kapoor (75-70) and Ridhima Dilawari (74-71), who, between them, have won six titles this season. Also tied for second with Kapoor and Dilawari was Durga Nittur (73-72) at 5-over 145. Overnight leaders Ananya Datar (71-75) and amateur Ojaswini Saraswat (71-76) slipped to fifth and sixth. Jasmine had three bogeys in the first six holes and then birdied the 8th, 14th and 18th to claw back to even par. Kapoor bogeyed the seventh and got back that shot on the 14th as scoring continued to be challenging at the Rambagh Club. Ridhima, meanwhile, followed her opening 74 with a one-over 71. She had an encouraging start to the round, including a birdie on the second. She dropped shots on the fifth and the seventh and then had one birdie and one bogey on the back nine for a 71. Durga also remained firmly in the hunt. After an opening 73, she carded a 72 to join Vani and Ridhima in second place. Her opening nine was particularly solid, with a 35, although a two-over back nine prevented her from taking a share of the lead. The second round also saw the first-round leaders lose ground. Ananya Datar, who had set the pace with a one-over 71 on Thursday, slipped to a five-over 75 and dropped to fifth at 146. She is now two shots behind Jasmine but remains close enough to mount a challenge. Amateur Ojaswini Saraswat also had a difficult day after beginning with a 71. She carded a six-over 76 to move to sixth at 147, three shots off the lead. Riya Jadon was in seventh place with rounds of 74-74, while Lavanya Jadon and Shweta Mansingh shared eighth at 149. Further down, Mannat Brar, Sneha Sharan, Amandeep Drall, Shagun Narain and Khushi Khanijau were tied for 10th at 150. -PTI

articles.title: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030 - The Hindu
articles.summary: KPMG sets up sports tech hub to unlock India’s $40-bn sports opportunity by 2030 The Hindu
articles.content: Bengaluru KPMG in India opened its Sports Technology Hub, a platform designed to help sports organisations in the country accelerate digital transformation, unlock new growth opportunities and build future-ready sporting ecosystems. The initiative is expected to bring together emerging technologies, industry expertise, and practical use cases to address evolving business and operational challenges in the sports industry. As the sports industry continued to evolve, organisations were increasingly leveraging technology to enhance fan experiences, improve athlete performance and strengthen commercial outcomes, KPMG officials said, adding, ``However, fragmented data, legacy infrastructure, operational inefficiencies and rising expectations for personalised experiences continue to hinder innovation.’’ The Sports Technology Hub in Bengaluru aims to address these challenges through practical solutions that sports organisations can evaluate and adopt. The hub was officially inaugurated by Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India, and P. T. Usha, President of the Indian Olympic Association, here on Friday. Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India, said, “Realising India’s potential in sports calls for innovation across the entire sports value chain. Our sports technology hub aims to bring industry expertise and technology together to help reshape how a sport is played, managed and experienced. As India strengthens its position on the global sports stage, technology will be central to building a more competitive, connected and future-ready sports ecosystem.” According to Prasanth Shanthakumaran, Partner and Head of Sports Sector, KPMG in India said, the hub showcases a range of technology-driven solutions, including AI-powered fan engagement platforms, smart stadium and venue management, athlete performance analytics, computer vision-based training and match insights, digital ticketing and loyalty solutions, and sponsorship measurement tools. It also incorporates capabilities in predictive maintenance, cybersecurity, sustainability and generative AI-enabled content creation to help sports organisations optimise operations and unlock new commercial opportunities. “The Sports Technology Hub brings together cutting-edge technologies such as AI, advanced analytics, computer vision, and digital platforms to address some of the most pressing challenges facing the sports industry today,’’ added Mr. Shanthakumaran. By showcasing practical, outcome-driven solutions, we aim to help sports organisations innovate faster, improve performance, and create more engaging experiences for fans, athletes, and partners, he further said. Designed as a collaborative platform, the Sports Technology Hub is expected to bring together sports federations, leagues, clubs, technology providers, startups and other industry stakeholders to explore and scale innovative solutions.

articles.title: India seek revenge against Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup final, eye record ninth title - India Today
articles.summary: India seek revenge against Pakistan in U19 Asia Cup final, eye record ninth title India Today
articles.content: India will have more than just a trophy on their minds when they take on arch-rivals Pakistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup 2026 final on Saturday, November 14, at Ministry Turf 2 in Al Amerat, Oman. The young Indian side will be eager to settle old scores, avenge their group-stage defeat and reclaim the continental crown after missing out on the title in the previous three editions.India are chasing a record-extending ninth U19 Asia Cup title, while defending champions Pakistan will be aiming to lift the trophy for the third time.There is also recent history to contend with. In last year's final in Dubai, Pakistan handed India a crushing 191-run defeat. Sameer Minhas was the chief architect of that victory, smashing a sensational 172 off 113 balls before Ali Raza followed it up with a four-wicket haul.The two teams have already faced each other in this edition, with Pakistan once again emerging victorious. Chasing 209, Pakistan were reduced to 61 for 5 before wicketkeeper-batter Hamza Zahoor produced a remarkable unbeaten century to turn the match on its head. His knock helped Pakistan pull off a three-wicket win, handing India their only defeat of the tournament so far.INDIA AND PAKISTAN DOMINATE SEMIFINALSBoth teams head into the final on the back of convincing semifinal victories. India registered an emphatic eight-wicket win over Afghanistan, with Ishan Sood leading the bowling effort with three wickets for 43 runs, while Aryan Savsani chipped in with two scalps.India made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 36.5 overs. Captain Lakshya Raichandani led from the front with a fluent 93, while Aaryavir Sehwag contributed 51. VK Vineeth remained unbeaten on 57 as India cruised into the final with 79 balls to spare.Pakistan were equally dominant against Bangladesh. After electing to bat, Bangladesh struggled against a disciplined bowling attack and were bowled out for 138 in 31.4 overs. Rizwanullah was the pick of the bowlers, claiming five wickets for 30 runs.Pakistan needed just 21.5 overs to chase down the target, losing only one wicket in the process. Hayam Khan scored 69, while Usman Khan remained unbeaten on 64 as the defending champions sealed a nine-wicket victory with 169 balls to spare.AARYAVIR, SOOD, AND HAMZA IN FOCUSFor India, Aaryavir Sehwag will be one of the key players to watch. The young opener, son of former India batter Virender Sehwag, has been in outstanding form, scoring 303 runs in four matches at an average of 101. His tally includes a century and two half-centuries, making him the tournament's leading run-scorer.India will also rely heavily on Ishan Sood, who has picked up 11 wickets in four matches. His ability to strike at crucial moments will be vital against a Pakistan batting line-up that has shown considerable depth. Captain Lakshya Raichandani's leadership and recent form will also be important, while Arjun Rajput could provide another valuable contribution with both bat and ball.Pakistan, meanwhile, have several match-winners of their own. Usman Khan has scored 238 runs in four matches and has been particularly effective at the top of the order. Hamza Zahoor will once again be a major threat with the bat, having already demonstrated his ability to turn a game around against India.Rizwanullah is another player India will need to watch closely. With 11 wickets, he is among the leading wicket-takers in the competition and has already shown his ability to dismantle opposition batting line-ups. Mohammad Sayyam and Ali Raza add further firepower to Pakistan's pace attack.INDIA HAVE A POINT TO PROVEWhile Pakistan will enter the final with the confidence of having beaten India in their last two U19 Asia Cup meetings, the defending champions will know that an India-Pakistan contest can quickly swing either way.For India, the challenge will be to put together a complete team performance rather than rely on individual brilliance. Their key players have stepped up at different stages of the tournament, but they will need consistent contributions across the batting order and bowling attack to get past Pakistan.The memories of last year's final in Dubai and the heartbreak of the group-stage defeat will provide India with extra motivation. They have an opportunity to end their title drought, reclaim the continental crown and make a statement against their fiercest rivals.Pakistan, meanwhile, will be determined to defend their crown and make it three consecutive U19 Asia Cup victories over India. With the trophy and bragging rights at stake, the stage is set for another high-stakes India-Pakistan final.WHEN TO WATCH INDIA VS PAKISTAN FINAL IN U19 ASIA CUP CLASHThe final between India and Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup will start at 10:30 AM IST and 9 AM local time.WHERE TO WATCH INDIA VS PAKISTAN FINAL IN U19 ASIA CUP CLASHSony Sports Network has the broadcasting rights for the U19 Asia Cup. Live Streaming of the match will be available on Sony LIV.SQUADS FOR INDIA VS PAKISTAN FINALIndia: Lakshya Raichandani (C), Aaryavir Sehwag, V.K. Vineeth, Yashbardhan Singh Chauhan (VC), Kushagra Ojha, Arjun Rajput, Manal Chauhan, Anvay Dravid (WK), Rajat Baghel (WK), V. Yashveer, Aryan Savsani, Mohit Ulva, Kavya Patel, Shavin Vinod, Ishan Sood.Pakistan: Farhan Yousuf (C), Abdul Qadir (WK), Abdul Subhan, Ahmed Hussain, Ali Raza, Hamza Zahoor (WK), Hasnain Abbas Dar, Hayam Khan, Huzaifa Ahsan, Jahangir Bilal, Mohammad Huzaifa, Mohammad Seyam, Niqab Shafiq, Rizwanullah, Usman Khan.- Ends

articles.title: More than sponsorship: How Odisha government is backing Indian hockey's rise - India Today
articles.summary: More than sponsorship: How Odisha government is backing Indian hockey's rise India Today
articles.content: For years, one name has remained synonymous with the rise of Indian hockey: Odisha. At a time when Indian hockey was struggling to find a main sponsor, the state stepped in and put its name on the jerseys of the national teams.What began as a sponsorship arrangement has since grown into a much bigger partnership, with Odisha emerging as one of the biggest pillars of support for the sport in the country. The state has since hosted major international tournaments and key matches for the Indian team with support for the sport being in abundance.INDIAN HOCKEY: FULL COVERAGEThat relationship has only grown stronger over the years. The Odisha government has continued the backing, going beyond sponsorship to ensure that the national teams receive the support they need and that the sport's development remains a priority.One of the most recent gestures came after India's men's and women's teams clinched gold medals at the Asian Games. The players were rewarded for their achievements, with each member of the teams receiving Rs. 11 lakh and every member of the support staff being awarded Rs. 5.5 lakh.The state also extended its sponsorship of Indian hockey until 2036, underlining its long-term commitment to the sport.But Odisha's contribution goes well beyond financial rewards or having its name on the national team's jersey. The state is looking to play a much bigger role in shaping the future of Indian hockey, from supporting elite players to building a stronger development structure at the grassroots.MAKING A DIFFERENCEAt the heart of Odisha's continued push for Indian hockey are Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and Sports Minister Suryabanshi Suraj. The duo have made a conscious effort to stay connected with the players, particularly ahead of major tournaments, while ensuring that the teams have access to top-class facilities.For the players, that personal connect has been just as important as the financial and infrastructural support. Mandeep Singh revealed how the Chief Minister regularly checks in with the team, both before and after major assignments."Whenever we travel for a major tournament, the Chief Minister also calls and speaks to the captain and the players. Even after the tournament, he gets in touch and asks how things went.""He also speaks to Hockey India and checks whether we are facing any difficulties or if anything is lacking. He wants to know if everything is fine and whether we need anything.""That kind of support and concern makes a big difference to the team," said Mandeep Singh while talking to India Today.Odisha has also steadily established itself as a home for Indian hockey. With Bhubaneswar and Rourkela emerging as major centres for the sport, the state has become a regular destination for domestic and international competitions. The infrastructure and continued investment have helped create an ecosystem where hockey can grow and players can thrive.Amit Rohidas, one of the finest hockey players to emerge from Odisha, believes the state's consistent backing has played a significant role in taking the sport forward."This has been extremely helpful for Indian hockey because when you have that kind of backing, the sport naturally grows. It benefits Hockey India as well as the players, because a lot of investment has to go into developing players.""Odisha government have continued to support Indian hockey. Whether it is the Pro League, international events or domestic tournaments such as the Hockey India League, the support has been there," said Rohidas.For Rohidas, however, the relationship goes beyond the support extended to the sport. The Indian defender also spoke about the warmth and familiarity that players share with the Chief Minister and the Sports Minister, making it easier for them to communicate their needs and discuss the future of hockey."Whenever we meet them, it feels like we are sitting with friends. We can openly discuss whatever we need or want to ask, and they also speak freely. There is no hesitation. We can sit comfortably and have a discussion.""That is something I really appreciate because, as a player, what you want is respect. When they give us that respect and importance, it means a lot," said Rohidas.FOCUS ON GRASSROOTSWhile Odisha has built a strong foundation for elite hockey, the next big challenge lies in ensuring that the pipeline of talent remains healthy. For Rohidas, that development is particularly close to home.Hailing from Sundargarh district, the Indian defender has seen the efforts being made to identify and nurture young players. He pointed to the establishment of training centres across the district as an important step towards creating a pathway for aspiring hockey players."Odisha has set up centres across 19 blocks in Sundargarh district, with coaches appointed to work at the grassroots level. From there, players can progress to the state level, where they receive guidance from different coaches, before eventually moving to the national and international levels," said Rohidas.But simply setting up centres is not enough. Rohidas believes the focus must remain on the quality of coaching and the time invested in young players. He stressed that every stage of the development pathway needs to function effectively if Odisha wants to keep producing players for the national team."We have to pay attention to this entire ladder of development. The foundation of that system is the coaches, and they play a very important role. If they do their jobs properly, players will emerge naturally."The defender also had a clear message for the state government, urging it to strengthen its grassroots efforts and ensure that the investment translates into opportunities for young players."My message would always be to focus more on grassroots development and ensure that the work is done with discipline.""We have a target of producing more young talent and having more players from Odisha in the national team. We need to concentrate on that. If we invest in the right areas, the results will come," said Rohidas.The message is clear. Odisha has already done much of the heavy lifting in giving Indian hockey financial stability, world-class infrastructure and a home for major tournaments. And now the focus will be on ensuring that the tradition of the sport continues in the state and more stars will come from there.- Ends

articles.content: India finish with 10 medals in Dakar, their second-best Youth Olympic Games haul after 2018. Gunjan and L. Ambekar Meetei win India's first-ever boxing gold medals at the Games. Dhinidhi wins two swimming bronzes as India claim maiden medals in swimming, beach wrestling and wushu. Swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu, the first Indian athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Youth Olympic Games, and the country's two gold-medal-winning boxers were among the standout performers as India concluded their campaign at the 2026 edition in Dakar, Senegal, with a haul of 10 medals. This was India's second-best performance at the Games, after the 2018 edition, when the country won 13 medals. Gunjan and L. Ambekar Meetei secured India's first-ever boxing gold medals at the Games, which serve as a breeding ground for potential champions. India also won three silver and five bronze medals across seven disciplines. Five of the medallists were Khelo India athletes (KIAs) — Tanvi Patri (badminton), Khushbu Rajakbhai (judo), Shourya Ambure (athletics), Gunjan (boxing) and Tirthank Pegu (swimming). Competing in 11 disciplines, Indian athletes won medals in seven, including the country's first-ever podium finishes in swimming, beach wrestling and wushu. In boxing, L Ambekar Meetei clinched gold in the men's 50kg category, while Gunjan won the women's 48kg title. Besides boxing's perfect campaign, with two gold medals, India registered breakthrough performances across several sports. Swimming was the country's most productive discipline, accounting for three of its 10 medals and delivering India's first-ever medals in the sport at the Youth Olympics. .U-19 Asia Cup: Meet Aaryavir, a Sehwag who wants to bat like Kohli. Tanvi won silver in the women's singles event, becoming the first Indian woman to claim a badminton medal at the Youth Olympics. Bengaluru swimmer Dhinidhi, meanwhile, won bronze in both the 100m and 200m freestyle events. In beach wrestling, Taniya secured silver, giving India its first-ever medal in the discipline at the Games. Dhinidhi qualified for the 200m freestyle final after clocking 56.80 seconds in the heats, the third-fastest time overall. She improved her timing by 0.53 seconds in the final, setting a national record and securing bronze. Although she had set her sights on gold, Dhinidhi took pride in the bronze, describing it as an important milestone in her journey. The podium finish has strengthened her resolve to pursue her dream of winning an Olympic medal, while also inspiring more girls to take up swimming — a discipline in which India has yet to establish itself at the highest level. In athletics, Shourya Ambure won bronze in the women's 100m hurdles, becoming the first Indian woman to win an athletics medal at the Youth Olympic Games. In wushu, Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu, a trainee at the Sports Authority of India's National Centre of Excellence (NCOE) in Imphal, won bronze in the women's Changquan combined event, securing India's first medal in the discipline at the Youth Olympics. . articles.title: Deepti Sharma bags second ICC Player of the Month award after Zimbabwe series heroics - India Today
articles.summary: Deepti Sharma bags second ICC Player of the Month award after Zimbabwe series heroics India Today
articles.content: India all-rounder Deepti Sharma has been named the ICC Women's Player of the Month for October 2026, earning the honour for the second time in her career. Deepti beat Bangladesh's Sobhana Mostary and Australia's Annabel Sutherland to claim the award after an impressive series against Zimbabwe at home.The 29-year-old played a crucial role in India's dominant white-ball campaign, contributing with both bat and ball across the three T20Is and three ODIs. She finished the month with 155 runs and seven wickets in six international matches as India remained unbeaten against Zimbabwe.“I’m pleased to win the ICC Women’s Player of the Month award," Deepti said."The series against Zimbabwe was a great one for us, and I’m proud of the way the team performed, especially the youngsters."Scoring a century was a particularly special moment for me, made even more meaningful as it contributed to a winning cause." The award marks another milestone in Deepti's career. She first won the ICC Women's Player of the Month honour in December 2023, following her outstanding performances against England and Australia. Nearly three years later, the experienced all-rounder has added a second monthly award to her collection.“I would like to thank the voting panel and fans for this recognition, as well as my teammates and coaches for their continued support," she added."I would like to dedicate this award to my fans across the world.”DEEPTI IMPRESSES AGAINST ZIMBABWEDeepti's contributions began in the T20I series, where she struck a quickfire 49 off 37 deliveries in the opening match in Raipur. Her innings helped India recover from a difficult position at 194 and set up a victory. She also picked up two wickets across the three-match series as India completed a 3-0 sweep.She carried that form into the ODI leg, picking up two wickets in the series opener before producing her standout performance in the second match in Vadodara.Batting at No. 6, Deepti smashed an unbeaten 106 off just 86 deliveries, striking 15 boundaries. It was her second ODI century and her first in the format since scoring 188 against Ireland in May 2017. She also claimed three wickets for 32 runs as India registered a 121-run victory to seal the series.Deepti's all-round contributions ensured she finished October among the standout performers in women's international cricket. Her second ICC monthly award is further recognition of her consistency and value to the Indian team.- Ends

articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur wants young India women to unleash their inner Vaibhav Sooryavanshi - India Today
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur wants young India women to unleash their inner Vaibhav Sooryavanshi India Today
articles.content: Harmanpreet Kaur has a message for India's young women cricketers: embrace the fearlessness and aggression that have made Vaibhav Sooryavanshi one of the most exciting young talents in the game. The India batter believes the teenager's approach can inspire the next generation of women cricketers to change the way the sport is played.She shared her thoughts in Jaipur on Friday, November 13, as she unveiled her wax statue. The statue will be installed at the Historical Museum inside Nahargarh Fort, where it will stand alongside those of legendary Indian cricketers MS Dhoni and Sachin Tendulkar."Yes, definitely, like right now he has set an example with the way he is playing cricket. And I'm sure that the new young girls coming up will also play aggressive cricket like this, and across the entire country and the entire world, they will change the image of women's cricket and try to play impressive cricket in the same way," Harmanpreet told reporters in Jaipur.The former India captain believes Sooryavanshi's fearless approach could encourage young girls to be more expressive and positive with the bat, while helping women's cricket develop a more attacking identity.SOORYAVANSHI'S RISE SETS THE TONEAt just 15, Sooryavanshi has already made a name for himself with his explosive batting. The Rajasthan Royals opener announced himself in the IPL in 2025, smashing a 101 off just 38 balls against Gujarat Titans. His century came off 35 deliveries, making him the youngest centurion in men's T20 cricket and one of the fastest to reach the landmark in IPL history.He continued to make headlines in 2026, scoring another IPL century — a 103 off 37 balls against Sunrisers Hyderabad. Earlier this year, Sooryavanshi also broke Shafali Verma's record to become the youngest Indian to play international cricket when he made his debut during the tour of England.Harmanpreet's comments come at a significant moment for Indian women's cricket. She led India to their maiden Women's ODI World Cup title in 2025, a landmark achievement that gave the team and the sport a major boost. Her wax statue in Jaipur is another recognition of her contribution to that historic campaign.Harmanpreet stepped down as India's captain across all three formats in October but remains part of the team as a player. She will next be in action on India's all-format tour of South Africa in December, where the teams will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is. The Test begins in Gqeberha on December 9, followed by the ODI series from December 16.- Ends

articles.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday highlighted India's rapid progress in astronomy, astrophysics and space technology, emphasising that scientific advancements and space exploration must ultimately serve humanity.Speaking in Mysuru after inaugurating COSMOS-Mysuru, India's first LED Dome Planetarium, Modi said India's space programme has consistently focused on improving the lives of its people."Humanity first" has been the guiding principle of India's space missions, the Prime Minister said, pointing to how satellite technology is being used for applications ranging from disaster warnings to railway operations and public safety.Highlighting India's achievements in space, Modi said the country has made rapid progress in astronomy and astrophysics, with new telescopes being installed and ambitious scientific missions expanding its capabilities. PM Modi watch a visual at the newly inaugurated Mysore planetarium. (Photo: PIB)He cited Chandrayaan-3's historic landing near the Moon's south pole, the Aditya-L1 mission becoming India's first dedicated space-based solar observatory and ISRO's Space Docking Experiment (SpaDeX), which demonstrated docking and undocking capabilities and made India the fourth country to achieve the feat.The Prime Minister also highlighted India's growing human spaceflight capabilities, noting that an Indian astronaut had travelled to the International Space Station (ISS) and conducted experiments that would contribute to the country's Gaganyaan programme.SPACE TECHNOLOGY FOR EVERYDAY LIFEModi stressed that India's space programme was not limited to scientific exploration but was also delivering practical benefits to citizens.He pointed to the use of satellite technology in providing fishermen with alerts about approaching cyclones and tracking their movements, helping improve maritime safety.Satellite-based systems are also being used to track trains in real time, through collaboration between ISRO and Indian Railways, improving railway operations and passenger information services.The Prime Minister said these applications demonstrated how investments in advanced space technology could translate into tangible public benefits.PRIVATE SECTOR AND YOUNG INNOVATORS TAKE CENTRE STAGEModi also highlighted the opening up of India's space sector to private participation, saying it had created new opportunities for entrepreneurs, startups and young innovators.Young Indians are now developing rockets, building satellites and working on technologies that were previously largely restricted to government space agencies.He also underlined the importance of nurturing scientific curiosity among school students through initiatives such as Atal Tinkering Labs, which encourage innovation and hands-on experimentation.The Prime Minister further referred to the One Nation One Subscription initiative, which aims to provide students, researchers and academic institutions access to international research journals and scientific publications.Modi said expanding access to scientific knowledge and research infrastructure was essential to building India's future innovation ecosystem.His remarks reinforced the broader message that India's expanding scientific and space capabilities must translate into opportunities, knowledge and solutions for society.- Ends

articles.content: Chennai TENNIS World Tennis League Returns for Season 5 in Bengaluru from December 17–20 The World Tennis League (WTL) will return for a fifth edition to Bengaluru. The four-day tennis spectacle will take place from December 17 to 20, 2026. The tournament will be played at the KSLTA, S.M. Krishna Tennis Stadium, bringing together leading international stars alongside India’s top players. Paula Badosa, Yuki Bhambri, Sumit Nagal, Dhakshineswar Suresh, Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi and Shrivalli Bhamidipaty will be back on the WTL court for the upcoming edition. “Last season was an exciting chapter for the World Tennis League, with an impressive mix of international talent and Indian players coming together to deliver some memorable tennis. As we move into Season 5, we are looking to build on that momentum, take the league to new audiences and continue raising the bar with every edition,” said co-founder Mahesh Bhupathi. - Team Sportstar SQUASH Om Semwal, Rathika Seelan and Sanya Vats advance in Singapore Classic squash Om Semwal, Rathika Seelan and Sanya Vats advanced to the second round of the Singapore Classic squash with contrasting victories on Wednesday, while Sandhesh Palanivel Ravikumar lost in the opener of the USD 15,000 PSA Challenger event. While men’s world No 149 Semwal rallied from 2-1 down to beat Singapore’s Aaron Liang 15-13, 6-11, 13-15, 11-9, 11-8, Rathika eased past Singapore’s Jayna Lim 11-7, 12-10, 11-9 and Sanya edged out Egypt’s Clara Dwerri 10-12, 11-6, 11-8, 11-5 in the women’s section. Men’s sixth seed Suraj Chand and women’s third seed Tanvi Khanna received first-round byes. - Team Sportstar GOLF Amateur Ojaswini shares lead with Ananya in Hero WPGT Amateur Ojaswini Saraswat landed a late eagle on her way to a one-over 71 to grab a share of the lead with Ananya Datar in the 14th leg of the Hero Women’s Professional Golf Tour in Jaipur on Thursday. The 13-year-old had become the youngest Indian ever and the second-youngest player in Ladies European Tour (LET) history to make the cut when she successfully made it to the weekend at the Hero Women’s Indian Open. Pre-tournament favourite and runner-up at the Hero Women’s Indian Open last month, Vani Kapoor was T-12 alongside Shagun Narain at 5-over 75. Neither of them had any birdies through the day. Amandeep Drall, Tvesa Malik, Seher Atwal and Sneha Sharan were in a tie for 14th at 6-over. - PTI Gill, Aman among four Indians lying T-38 in Manila Four of the seven Indian golfers playing in the Philippine Open shot 1-over 71 and were placed Tied-38th after the first round of the tournament in Manila on Thursday. The quartet included Pukhraj Singh Gill, who has already secured his Asian Tour card for 2027, Aman Raj, Shaurya Bhattacharya and Anirban Lahiri. Gill had five birdies against two bogeys and two double bogeys, while Lahiri had two birdies against three bogeys, and Aman Raj had three birdies against four bogeys. Shaurya had one birdie and two bogeys. - PTI Teenager Danish Verma takes one-shot lead over Bhullar, Kapur in Hyderabad golf Fifteen-year-old Danish Verma grabbed the sole lead with an impressive 11-under total after the second round of the Phoenix Invitational Hyderabad Golf here on Thursday. Playing at the Vooty Golf County for the first time, the Green Fuels Vizag Dolphins GC golfer carded a six-under 66 after opening with a five-under 67 to move one shot clear of an experienced field heading into the final round. Veterans Gaganjeet Bhullar (66-68) and Shiv Kapur (68-66), along with emerging golfer Harshjeet Singh Sethie (67-67), were tied second at 10-under. Verma, who became the youngest Indian professional earlier this season, had a late bogey on the 17th but remained pleased with his performance. “I struck the ball very well throughout the round. Yes, I did miss a couple of putts under 10 feet, but overall, a great round,” he said. - PTI CRICKET MPL franchise Ratnagiri Jets launches official cricket academy Ratnagiri Jets, two-time Maharashtra Premier League (MPL) champions, have announced the launch of their first official cricket academy in partnership with Silver Birch Vision Sports Academy in Pune. The academy is designed to bridge the gap between grassroots potential and professional cricket through a structured development pathway spanning players aged seven and above, including the Under-14, Under-16, Under-19 and Under-23 categories. Ratnagiri Jets recently conducted Under-16 and Under-19 talent trials, attracting over 700 aspiring cricketers. The new academy formalises this commitment into a year-round development programme, with plans to establish additional academies across key regions of Maharashtra. - Team Sportstar Jemimah Rodrigues becomes brand ambassador of Hero and Vida Indian cricketer Jemimah Rodrigues has signed up to be the brand ambassador of Hero Moto Corp. and Vida Dot World. The 26-year-old batter recently returned to the India squad for the South Africa tour after recovering from a hamstring issue. - Team Sportstar MOTORSPORT CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship 2026 resumes on November 14–15 Kari Motor Speedway is ready to host Round 2 of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship 2026 on November 14–15, with the opening round’s winners now wearing targets on their backs. The most unpredictable class of Round 1 was the LGB Formula 4, which produced a different winner in each race. Vadodara’s Kabir Sahoch left nothing to chance, winning all three races by margins of 2.298, 3.218 and 1.793 seconds in the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup in the amateur category. The Professionals produced three different winners across the three races. The weekend will also see action in the JK Tyre Levitas Cup, the JK Tyre Novice Cup and the Super Saloon. - Team Sportstar BLIND CRICKET BCCI sponsors air fare for India’s visually challenged cricket squad Durga Rao Tompaki will lead a 17-member visually challenged Indian cricket team that was given a send-off in New Delhi on Thursday ahead of the Asia Cup, scheduled to be held in Dhaka from November 15 to 20. The BCCI has extended its support to the team by sponsoring round-trip air tickets from New Delhi to Dhaka. “We believe that cricket should provide opportunities for everyone to participate and excel,” BCCI honorary secretary Devajit Saikia said, wishing the team success. The squad includes players from Gujarat, Delhi, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana and Karnataka. India will open their campaign against Sri Lanka on November 15 before taking on Pakistan on November 17. They will face hosts Bangladesh on November 19. The final is scheduled for November 20. - PTI GYMNASTICS Odisha AM/NS India gymnastics athletes excel at CBSE National Gymnastics Championship 2026 Athletes from the Odisha AM/NS India Gymnastics High Performance Centre (Odisha AM/NS India GHPC), Bhubaneswar, and the Odisha AM/NS India Gymnastics Grassroots Centre, Rourkela, delivered an impressive performance at the CBSE National Gymnastics Championship 2026 held in Pune, Maharashtra. Pritti Jhankaar won two gold medals in the All-Around and Balance Beam events in the U-17 category. In the U-11 category, Rose Minzi secured two gold medals in the All-Around and Balance Beam events and a silver medal in Floor Exercise. articles.title: 134 Maharashtra government hospitals still without fire safety NOCs after Amravati Hospital fire - Medical Dialogues
articles.summary: 134 Maharashtra government hospitals still without fire safety NOCs after Amravati Hospital fire Medical Dialogues
articles.content: Mumbai: Fire safety compliance remains pending at 134 government hospitals across Maharashtra, even after a state-wide inspection drive launched following a devastating blaze at the Amravati District Women’s Hospital that claimed the lives of three newborns, while 36 others were rescued. A report by the state Public Health Department indicates that several public health institutions are yet to meet the required safety standards. Of the 527 functional government health facilities, 59 are still without installed fire safety systems, while 134 have not secured the mandatory Fire Safety No Objection Certificates (NOCs), Hindustan Times reported.Also Read:Amravati Hospital Fire: No lapse in fire safety audits, says District Magistrate In the aftermath of the incident, the state government had directed authorities to conduct immediate audits of fire safety arrangements, electrical installations, building infrastructure and hospital equipment in government, private and charitable healthcare facilities. According to the Daily, the department’s data show that fire safety audits have been completed at 511 facilities, with inspections pending at the remaining 16. However, the completion of inspections has not resulted in corresponding improvements in compliance. Fire safety equipment has been installed at 468 facilities, while only 393 have obtained the required NOCs. The state has also conducted 1,757 fire mock drills. Officials pointed out that an audit is only the initial stage of the process, after which hospitals must address identified shortcomings, install necessary equipment, complete infrastructure-related work and secure approval from the authorised fire department. Pune district highlights the gap between audit completion and obtaining official clearance. All 31 public health facilities in the district have undergone fire safety audits and installed the required systems, but only four have received Fire NOCs. Consequently, 27 facilities are still awaiting mandatory certification, reports The Daily. According to the department, the remaining certificates will be secured once pending work is completed. The situation has raised concerns over why the facilities continue to lack official clearance despite completing inspections and installing fire safety arrangements. Beed is another district facing considerable delays. Although fire safety audits have been conducted at all 18 public health facilities, installation work has been completed at just one, leaving 17 without the required systems. The district has prepared an estimate of ₹24.39 crore for installing fire safety arrangements at the district hospital and its subordinate healthcare facilities. However, the proposal is awaiting government approval, holding up the implementation process. Chandrapur is also struggling to complete the necessary installations, with 13 of its 14 hospitals yet to put fire safety systems in place. Only one facility has completed the work. Against a sanctioned allocation of ₹899.02 lakh, expenditure so far stands at ₹247.07 lakh. The department has requested the release of the outstanding ₹651.95 lakh from the District Planning and Development Committee and the Directorate of Health Services to take the work forward. There have been similar instances of shortcomings in infrastructure from other districts also. As far as the Rural Hospital in Bhandara is concerned, work on submersible pumps is still pending, though fire water tanks have been installed. In Gadchiroli, other than two facilities, all of them have been served final Fire NOCs, and the District Hospital along with Women's hospitals have only gained provisional clearances. Ratnagiri has completed its fire safety system within only five days in all the 12th hospitals, while seven are still in progress. As for Sindhudurg, other than two sub-district hospitals at Kankavli and Sawantwadi, installation has yet to be completed in nine facilities. Installation work remains underway at six out of 19 facilities in Buldhana, while work at the district hospital in Nandurbar is still incomplete. Ahmednagar and Kolhapur have each reported that installation is still pending at two facilities. Dr Abhjit More, a health activist associated with Jan Aarogya Abhiyan, told Hindustan Times that the same safety standards that private facilities are supposed to adhere to have not been adopted in its own hospitals. “Even the Supreme Court has repeatedly emphasised the need to give priority to fire safety. The government makes fire safety compliance mandatory for private hospitals and includes it in their registration provisions. However, when it comes to its own facilities, there is serious negligence.
